doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Hamilton as a bargain: professors, Dean Tolles and Storyville
summary: He felt Hamilton was a bargain with small classes; Dean Tolles sent him to Harvard Business School but he skipped out to hear Ruby Braff and Sonny Greer at Storyville.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: When you got out of Hamilton do you think, did you feel like you had had a bargain at this college? And I’m sort of asking that in the relationship of what it cost back then?

I can’t remember what my dad, who was a dentist, and what he paid. It was a few thousand I guess. A bargain. Yeah I think I thought I’ve gotten an awful lot. I was impressed, the college was small, three or four hundred people when I came up here. And the ratio of faculty to students was terrific. We had some classes with four and five people in it. And loved those teachers, those professors. Paul Parker, who became the pianist in the Alumni All-Stars, was a dear man who became very friendly and he would come down to my house and painted pictures of my boats and things like that. It is a wonderful school. I can’t imagine how I could have been as happy or as well prepared for life anyplace, and I loved Dean Tolles. Everybody loved Dean Tolles. He tried to make me a businessman. He thought I would have the talent to go to Harvard business school and make a big splash in the business world. But I knew I didn’t have it. So he sent me to Boston to go to Harvard and take some interviews in the Harvard business school. I spent one day. I was supposed to go three days. And after the first day I cut out and I went to Storyville to hear the jazz bands that were playing there. Ruby Braff, you know who Ruby Braff, the cornet? And Sonny Greer was the drummer. What bands. So I had a good time going for my interview but I didn’t get asked to go to the school and I didn’t want to go.
